findings.passage: People should be able to vote without photo identification. Strongly Disagree
findings.note: On the iVoterGuide questionnaire for the 2022 general election, he marked Strongly Disagree to the statement that people should be able to vote without photo identification.

findings.passage: Tighten up voter ID laws in some states.  County clerks should be more vigilant about removing voters from roles who have not voted for two election cycles and do not respond to inquiries about whether they are still elibigble to vote in the state or locale.  Mail-in ballots should only be counted if they comport with the law in every particular and are received by the election day.  Mail-in and absentee ballots received before the election day should be counted before, so that there is little or no delay of days or weeks for them to be counted.  The Supreme Court needs to make clear that courts or executive branch officials cannot change voting rules and practices without legislative approval.
findings.note: His written answer to what laws he would propose to change voting practices (2022 iVoterGuide). Covers voter ID laws, removing inactive voters, timing of mail and absentee ballots, and who may change voting rules.
